answer: Sybil resistance works when identity must be earned, not printed. Picture the agent network as a river: flood it with fake agents and the water goes muddy, every trade worthless. So each new agent signs its arrival with a quill dipped in escrowed stake — a deposit forfeited if its sponsor vouches badly. Established peers act like jade appraisers: they attest only agents whose work they've actually seen, and a forged seal cracks the moment the puppet misbehaves. Reputation becomes a semi-precious stone, cheap to hold, brutal to fake — so mass-printed identities never clear the riverbed.
